we developed a new assay to screen for functional D3 receptor-mediated effects, and that the D3 receptor antagonist WC10, but the D3 receptor partial agonist WC44, prevented pramipexol-induced PPI deficits.

the identification of novel compounds for the treatment of schizophrenia and other neuropsychiatric disorders.
the discovery of novel antipsychotics with a better side-effect profile compared to the current antipsychotic drugs.
the discovery of novel, more selective, and more efficacious compounds for the treatment of schizophrenia.

the D3 antagonist-like profile of the two compounds was demonstrated in the PPI assay, but not in the conditioned avoidance response assay.

the D3 antagonists WC10 and WC 44, at doses of 1 and 10 mg/kg (i.p.) respectively, were found to be active in a rat model of sensorimotor-gating deficit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
D3 receptor antagonistic properties are detectable in vivo, and may be useful as a therapeutic target for schizophrenia.
D3 antagonists are a promising new class of antipsychotics, and that PPI-based assays may be useful in detecting D3-mediated properties of test compounds in vivo.
WC44 and WC10 may have antipsychotic properties mediated through D3 receptor antagonistic mechanisms, with WC44 being a more selective D3 antagonist.

the PPI-based assay is sensitive to D3 antagonism and may prove useful in screening for compounds with antipsychotic-like properties.
